task_name: Project detection (package manager, script, port, framework)

concerns_addressed: Unknown packageManager prefix ignored (falls to lockfile): consistent with A2 prefix set npm|pnpm|yarn|bun; tested with deno@2.0.0. Accepted.
-p matched only with whitespace: matches spec literal '-p N'; avoids -p=... ambiguity. Accepted.
ng matched without requiring serve: spec says '@angular/cli (ng serve)'; looser than spec, Minor.
@sveltejs/kit deps-only: it has no command token, so command-first is vacuous; tested. Accepted.
Cycle 2 RED partly from a crash: process observation only, no code impact; final tests cover parsing behaviour. Accepted.

strengths: detect.ts is pure: no imports, no fs, no process.*, no new dependencies; package.json untouched
Detection type matches the task contract exactly (field names and types); scriptText documented as raw

52 tests pass in src/init; tsc --noEmit clean; every Story A scenario has a test (earliest-port, invalid ports 0/70000/$PORT/abc, framework table, tokens-before-deps, unknown 3000, packageManager+pmMajor, wrong-typed packageManager, fallback reasons, BOM)
Regexes use boundary prefixes: MY_PORT=, --preserve, --pport, --public do not false-match (probed and tested)
Property test exercises wrong-typed fields, BOM, and asserts port/script/pm invariants
Small file (179 lines), no function over 50 lines, no triplicated logic

issues.description: Port VALUE captures any non-whitespace except ;&|, so a closing paren or quote glued to the number invalidates a real explicit port: '(vite --port 3000)' and 'vite --port "4000"' fall back to the framework default. Consider also excluding ')' and quotes from VALUE or trimming them.
'ng' command token matches without requiring 'serve' (e.g. 'ng build', 'echo ng' report @angular/cli 4200); spec A3 says '@angular/cli (ng serve)'.
Framework command match follows FRAMEWORKS table order, not script position ('vite build && next dev' reports vite). Spec is silent; acceptable.

scripts that is not an object yields reason 'no-script' (A8 lists it separately but the Detection reason set has no distinct value); matches the task contract. A shell comment 'node a.js # PORT=9' yields explicit 9. Both are acceptable edge behaviour.
